entries.reason: The recipe build models the docs body by hand; the capture reads the host page's body rule, under its own name.
The page's body rule and Fuse's base layer on it, as the browser applies them.
Tailwind's preflight and Fuse's base layer on `<html>`, as the browser applies them.
Tailwind's preflight, which the capture page loads as the docs host does; its resets drop or read as the zero they set.
Fuse's base layer, which the recipe build modelled only for the border color: box sizing, zero border, margin and padding.
The browser's default style for the element, which the recipe build modelled only for `display`.

CSS clips nothing here (`overflow` is `visible` initially, CSS Overflow 3 §3) and the set's root casts no shadow in any cell, so the capture-backed root leaves its layers unclipped, and a ring at its edge shows as in the browser. A root that casts a shadow still clips, since Figma draws a spread only from a clipping frame (PR2).

The recipe definition modelled the host page's type on `<html>` by hand. The capture reads preflight's `line-height: 1.5` on `<html>`, and the build adds the browser's initial `medium` font size, 16px, which no rule declares. The root inherits both, as the `html` rows show.

The `<li>` is a list item with no marker, its resolved `list-style-type` and `list-style-image` `none`, so it lays out as the block box it is around its one layer: a vertical auto layout from its start, where the recipe build drew a centred row. A frame that hugs its one layer draws it the same in either direction and alignment.

`Pagination.Root` holds one child, its content, which `:not(:last-child)` never matches, so no element wins the class's declarations, as the class's row says.

A class whose state no cell of the matrix shows, which the recipe build dropped under the definition's hand-written facts or omissions. A manifest holds neither, so the capture lists it as unshown, named here, until the matrix shows its state or the kit decides it.
